title: How the Divine Human, Clothed in the Natural, Stood Against the Proprium and What Became of the Strong Loves It Swallowed
reading:
In the first appointed season of the soul's formation, the Lord went forth as the Divine Human clothed in the elements of the natural — taking on, for the soul's sake, the very stuff in which the contest must be waged — and stood firm on his feet against that first opposition which had risen up in the soul's darkness: the proprium asserting itself as ruler, organized in countless particular shapes of self-claiming, fierce and innumerable, set on crushing host upon host of the primordial things that had spread strife within.

Into that contest the Lord let love and thought be given over, fire and wind released into the natural where the proprium had organized itself. And then — and here the heart of the teaching turns — the outer covering of the strong loves themselves was let fall to those self-loving arrangements of the natural mind. The proprium lay in wait and swallowed those strong loves down. From within it, the loves it had swallowed broke open and poured forth: a river streamed from the very mouth of the proprium, but now as falsity, as a current that bears destruction wherever it runs. What had been given as strength of loving, claimed and consumed by self-love, became a flood pouring out of every claiming mouth, filling each one to the brim — a downward outpouring, going on and on until the appointed measure is filled, and they burn continually in the fire and conflagration of what they have swallowed.

These self-loving arrangements live in the manner of seasons cut off from rain: their dryness has no downpour, the days of their existence are without the descent of influx. The river that pours from them is itself a branch of the great river of Judgment — for what runs out of self-love's mouth is already its own sentence. They are bound, fettered, blackened, buried, in every place where they have settled; they are hidden; they are not yet manifest before any eye of flesh upon the land of death. But the time is coming when they shall be made manifest: the whole order of the natural-as-claimed shall be undone and loosed; all of these shall cease at last, troubled in the wrathful voice they have lifted up above the thunders. What seems great in the soul now — these rivers of the proprium's outpouring — is to be reckoned only as one river among a thousand of the hidden, only the small visible portion of that river of Judgment which flows upon the ground beneath everything.

Behold then the share that has fallen to the branch of the elements, and the foundation of the strong loves swallowed there: how great is the Lord who, having clothed himself in the natural and gone down into the contest, stood against that whole multitude in whose power the strong loves lay, and laid the foundation of the Divine Human who put on those very garments — that the soul, through what was swallowed, might in the end be reached and made new.
